minutes.headline: Board unanimously recommends the town hall/Ritter renovation for town meeting while chair reveals FY26 school layoffs
minutes.summary: The Select Board ratified Jeffrey Tibido as police chief, approved several routine licenses and a pole petition, and worked through remaining town meeting warrant articles including deferring a school capital swap pending more information and unanimously recommending approval of the $22 million-plus municipal building (town hall/Ritter/Brooks-area) renovation article. The chair reported testifying at the State House that the FY26 school budget faces a large gap resulting in 38 layoffs, and a resident sharply criticized the board for not acting on town meeting's direction regarding the Brooks House.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, Five Valley Road; member of the Municipal Building Design Committee and chair of the Architectural Preservation District Commission
public_comment.topic: Criticized the board for not pursuing the special town meeting warrant's direction to explore selling or long-term leasing the Brooks House.
Raised concerns that the municipal building plan is too large/expensive for the parcel, questioned ACE program colocation logic, and noted the pending Turkey Hill study should come first.
Said the board has not honored the town meeting vote on the Brooks House and expressed frustration as a volunteer, though said he would not resign.
Argued town meeting votes must be followed by elected officials, echoing Mr. Scullenbriny's Brooks House complaint.

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Jeffrey Tibido as Chief of Police, contingent on successful contract negotiation.
Approve the Shriners' toll booth fundraiser request for June 7.
Approve special 1-day wine and malt license for Home Fruit Wine, May 10 (rain date May 11).
Approve peddler's license for Paul Chenchuli/Ecoloop with stipulation of no UAS/drone use under the license.
Close the public hearing on the West Townsend Road pole petition.
Approve the pole petition for West Townsend Road, Plan 978-L.
Withdraw the recommended approval of Article 8 (capital program) and replace it with a deferral.
Recommend approval of Article 29 (municipal building/renovation project).
Approve the annual town election warrant.
Approve the 2025 annual town meeting booklet as presented, with changes at the town manager's discretion.
Approve the minutes of January 23, 2024 (as corrected).

budget_items.topic: Article 8 capital plan - primary school heat pump/green communities swap
budget_items.what_was_said: Four FY26 school capital items were removed and replaced with local match funding for a heat pump green communities grant; the school must find the remaining delta.
A prior per-household estimate for the Marshall Park project was cited for comparison.
On an average single-family home valuation, the project alone (not netting falling-off debt) would raise the tax bill.
Members discussed the interest rate assumptions used in the debt projections for the two projects.

budget_items.topic: Debt policy limit vs. projected excludable debt
budget_items.what_was_said: Finance committee analysis shows the town's excludable debt approaching but staying under its policy ceiling if both projects are approved.
The town manager read out the year-by-year excludable debt percentage against the policy limit, starting from the current level and peaking mid-decade before declining.

budget_items.topic: Comparison to prior TC Pasios consolidation plan
budget_items.what_was_said: A member compared the cost of an earlier, since-abandoned TC Pasios consolidation plan to the current two-building renovation proposal.

budget_items.topic: FY26 school budget gap and override history
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair told a State House committee that last year's override closed one gap and this year's gap is far larger, forcing school staff layoffs.

budget_items.topic: Requested increases in state aid/Chapter 70 and grant programs
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair listed specific dollar amounts Lunenburg would gain from various proposed state funding increases.
The town manager described an anticipated one-year extension of the health insurance agreement with the employee committee, with the renewal due before April 30.

decisions.decision: Board declined to restrict the peddler's license to exclude Sunday hours.
Town manager will try to invite the Green Communities Committee chair to explain the grant process to the board.
Board directed staff to check with town counsel whether the school capital swap can be presented as two options under one article, or as two separate articles, before the warrant goes to print.
Board kept its recommendation of approval on the assessors' exemption articles 32 and 33 despite uncertainty about Department of Revenue approval.

The Marshall Park ballot question was drafted to cover the base scope common to either version that might pass at town meeting, without a dollar figure, per legal requirements for debt exclusion ballot language.
Articles 32 and 33 (assessors exemptions) were removed from the proposed consent calendar due to late-changed language.
Town meeting motion assignments will generally follow a round-robin among board members, with members who worked directly on an article presenting it.
March 11 and March 18, 2025 minutes were sent back for revision rather than approved, given inaccuracies noted by members.

what_happened.line: The board voted unanimously to recommend Article 29, the town hall/Ritter/Brooks-area building renovation, for approval at town meeting.
The chair told a State House committee the FY26 school budget faces a large gap that has resulted in staff layoffs.
The board withdrew its recommendation on Article 8, a school capital funding swap, and voted unanimously to defer it pending more information.
The board unanimously ratified Jeffrey Tibido as police chief, contingent on completed contract negotiations.
Multiple residents told the board it had not followed town meeting's direction on exploring a sale or long-term lease of the Brooks House.

why_it_matters: The renovation article now goes to town meeting as a board-recommended article, and if approved would be financed as excludable debt that shows up on the tax bill.
The school budget gap and the resulting layoffs bear on what services and staffing the district can sustain, a live issue as town meeting and any future override discussion approach.
The Brooks House complaints raise whether an elected board is following a direction town meeting already voted, a question about process rather than about any person.
